h1: The 6 Best Privacy Screens for Dell Monitors in 22, 24 and 27 Inch Sizes, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Dell Monitor Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 privacy screens for Dell monitors in 22, 24 and 27 inch sizes, with 16:9 and 16:10 options and one-sheet or two-pack deals.
summary: The 2-pack 24 inch magnetic privacy screen that lists Dell compatibility is our top pick for the common Dell office monitor, since it names the brand and adds a quick-release magnet mount. The Peslv 27 inch two-pack is the best choice for larger Dell displays, the 27 inch two-pack with a blue-light filter adds a coating, and the Vxaop is the pick for 16:10 panels that many business monitors use.
intro: Dell makes some of the most common office monitors in the world, and that is exactly what makes buying a privacy filter confusing. The same 24 inch label covers panels in both 16:9 and 16:10 shapes, and a sheet cut for one will not cover the other. Shoppers who search by brand and diagonal alone often get a filter that leaves a visible strip bare.

So this ranking starts with shape and size. We reviewed six privacy screens sized for typical Dell monitors, covering 22, 24 and 27 inch panels, using their listings and compatibility lines, and ranked them on fit clarity, attachment style and pack value. None of these filters is made by Dell, and only one listing names Dell by brand, so check your model's exact dimensions on the maker's spec page before ordering.

products.name: 2-Pack 24 Inch Magnetic Computer Privacy Screen for Monitor, Lists Dell Compatibility
products.verdict: A magnetic 24 inch two-pack that names Dell compatibility and swaps off in seconds.
products.description:
This listing is a pair of magnetic privacy screens for 24 inch, 16:9 monitors, and it names Dell compatibility on the page. It falls in the $50 to $100 bracket for the two sheets.

It wins because a seller that calls out Dell by name is at least aware of the fit question, which most generic listings skip. Magnetic attachment also suits office life, since you can pull the sheet off for a screen share and snap it back afterward, and the second sheet covers a dual-monitor desk. The caution is that the 16:9 shape excludes the 16:10 Dell panels, so confirm your aspect ratio first.

Buy it for a 24 inch Dell office monitor with a standard 16:9 panel. Skip it if your Dell is 16:10 or if you want a coated filter.

products.name: Peslv 2-Pack 27 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9
products.verdict: A removable two-pack for 27 inch 16:9 monitors, with a clear size and ratio on the page.
products.description:
Peslv sells this removable two-pack of privacy screens for 27 inch monitors in 16:9. The listing is in the $50 to $100 bracket and keeps to the essentials of size, ratio and pack count.

It ranks second since 27 inch Dells are common in design, finance and engineering offices, and a clearly stated size and shape is the key for those buyers. The pair gives you a spare for another desk. It sits behind the top pick because it does not mention Dell directly and offers no quick-release mount, so removal is a slower job, and it trails a bit on features.

Choose it if you run one or two 27 inch Dell monitors and want a clean, no-frills fit. Skip it if your panel is 16:10.
products.idealFor: One or two 27 inch Dell displays.

products.name: Peslv 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9
products.verdict: The 24 inch sibling of the 27 inch Peslv pair, with the same simple removable design.
products.description:
This Peslv listing is the 24 inch version of the 27 inch pair, sold as two removable sheets for 16:9 monitors. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket and, like its sibling, keeps the details short.

Third place follows from competition inside the same size. The magnetic pair above does more with its listing, naming Dell and giving a quick-release mount, whereas this one sells on simplicity. Two sheets still make it good value for a pair of side-by-side monitors, and a removable design means you can clean the screen without fuss.

Buy it if you have two 24 inch Dell monitors and want a simple pair. Skip it if you want faster removal or an explicit Dell reference.
cons: No Dell reference in the listing
Slower to take off than magnets
products.skipIf: You want a magnetic quick release.

products.name: 2 Pack 27 Inch Computer Monitor Privacy Screen with Blue Light Filter
products.verdict: A 27 inch two-pack that combines privacy with blue-light filtering for the $25 to $50 tier.
products.description:
This 27 inch two-pack for 16:9 monitors combines privacy filtering with a blue-light filter. It lands in the $25 to $50 bracket, which makes it the cheapest pair here.

Fourth place reflects its value. Two 27 inch sheets for that price is a strong deal, and the blue-light layer gives a slightly warmer picture that some people prefer during long evenings. It does not name Dell and offers little other detail, so it relies on your own measurements to confirm the fit. Blue-light filtering is a comfort feature, not a medical one, and it will shift how colors look.

Pick it if you want two 27 inch sheets at the lowest price. Skip it if you do color-sensitive work, since the tint changes color balance.

products.name: Vxaop 2-Pack 22 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter, 16:10
products.verdict: A 22 inch pair cut for the taller 16:10 shape found on many business monitors.
products.description:
The Vxaop is a two-pack of 22 inch privacy filters in a 16:10 aspect ratio, priced in the $25 to $50 bracket. It is the only option here for a taller panel shape.

Fifth place comes from its narrow audience. If you have a 22 inch 16:10 monitor, which is a shape many business-grade displays have used, this is nearly your only fit in the ranking and the pair is an excellent value. If you have a modern 16:9 screen it will not fit at all. That makes it a precise tool rather than a general recommendation.

Buy it if your Dell is a 22 inch 16:10 model. Skip it otherwise, and confirm your resolution and size before ordering.
pros: Two sheets at a low price

products.name: SightPro 27 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: A single 27 inch, 16:9 filter from an established brand, at the $25 to $50 tier.
products.description:
This is a single SightPro privacy filter for 27 inch, 16:9 monitors, listed in the $25 to $50 bracket. SightPro has been in the filter market for years and the listing is simple.

Sixth place is mostly about pack size. A single sheet costs about as much as a pair of the other 27 inch options, so unless you only have one monitor and prefer a familiar name, the pairs give more for the money. The filter itself does the standard job of narrowing the viewing angle.

Choose it for a single 27 inch Dell display where brand familiarity matters. Skip it if you have a second monitor, since the two-packs cost less per sheet.

whatMatters.detail: Dell sells both 16:9 and 16:10 panels, and sometimes the same diagonal comes in both. A 16:9 sheet on a 16:10 screen leaves a bare strip. Look up your model on the maker's spec page and match the ratio exactly.

A 24 inch label can describe a 23.8 inch panel, and a 27 inch screen may measure slightly different. Most filters allow a small tolerance, but a sheet that is too short exposes the edge. Compare the listing size to your own measurement.

Magnetic, hanging and tab-mounted designs behave differently on thin Dell bezels. A magnet lets you remove the sheet quickly, while a plain removable sheet may need more care. Choose by how often you need a clear screen.

Every privacy filter dims the image and narrows the viewing angle. A blue-light layer adds a warm tint on top of that. If you edit photos or video, choose a removable filter and take it off for color work.

Most offices run at least two monitors, so a two-pack usually costs less per sheet than two singles. A spare also helps if one sheet is damaged during removal. Count your screens before you pick a pack.

faq.q: How do I know which Dell privacy screen fits my monitor?
faq.a: Find your exact model number on the back of the monitor, then check the maker's spec page for the diagonal and aspect ratio. Match both to the filter listing. Dell uses several panel shapes, so the brand name alone is not enough.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a Dell privacy filter?
faq.a: Ordering by diagonal alone and ignoring the aspect ratio. A 16:9 sheet will not cover a 16:10 Dell. Measure the visible screen area if you are unsure.

faq.q: Is the magnetic two-pack worth it over a plain pair?
faq.a: If you share your screen or present, yes, because removing and replacing the sheet takes seconds. For a screen that stays private all day, a plain pair does the same job.

faq.q: How do I install a privacy filter?
faq.a: Clean the screen, align the sheet with the top edge and let it settle flat. Smooth any bubbles toward the edges with a soft cloth. A magnetic sheet snaps into place once aligned.

faq.q: How should I clean the sheet?
faq.a: Use a dry microfiber cloth for dust and a barely damp one for smudges. Avoid sprays, which can seep behind the sheet. Store spare sheets flat in a folder.

faq.q: Will a filter work with my Dell monitor's built-in features?
faq.a: It sits in front of the panel, so it does not affect ports or the stand. It does reduce brightness, so you may need to turn up the display. Ambient light sensors, if any, may react to the dimmer view.

finalTake: For a typical 24 inch Dell office monitor, the 2-pack magnetic privacy screen that lists Dell compatibility is the best choice here. Owners of 27 inch panels should look to the Peslv pair, while the Vxaop is the right answer for 22 inch 16:10 screens. Confirm your aspect ratio on the spec page before you order, since that one check prevents the most common return.
